skills.name: ad-angle-miner
skills.description: Research supported advertising promises from a specific buyer's context, current product facts, customer language and observed ads. Turn them into static, video or copy ideas; match video ideas to actual recipes and save a product-scoped angle bank for write-video-ad-script. Product-led discovery can use verified facts without reviews. Reference persistence and reach are observations, not proof of performance.

skills.name: ad-campaign-analyzer
skills.description: Analyze ad campaign performance data (Google, Meta, LinkedIn) to identify what's working, what's wasting budget, and specific cut/scale/test recommendations. Runs statistical analysis, funnel diagnostics, and multi-channel budget reallocation with specific dollar-amount shift recommendations and scenario modeling.

skills.name: ad-lead-quality-analyzer
skills.description: For paid lead-gen and participant-recruitment ads, replaces vanity CPA with true CAC per qualified lead by joining ad-platform data with downstream funnel events, surfaces tracking gaps, and classifies every creative into Scale / Keep / Investigate / Cut.

skills.name: ad-management-intake
skills.description: The intake stage of a Meta ad harness. Researches the brand first, states what it assumes, and asks only what it cannot infer and what would change money, claims or legal exposure if guessed wrong — at most four questions a turn, in plain business language. Writes the brand's stable facts (ads/brand.md), the campaign brief, and a log of what was asked vs assumed. Use it when someone wants to run Meta ads and the brand's ad facts are not yet recorded.

features: research first, then only the questions a wrong guess would make expensive
at most four questions a turn, in plain business language
states every assumption out loud before writing it down
writes the brand facts, the campaign brief and a log of what was asked vs assumed
corrections update one fact without re-interviewing
metadata.example_prompt: Help me set up Meta ads for my shop. Ask me only what you really need.

skills.name: ad-policy-check
skills.description: Checks paid ads against the ad platform's rules (Meta, TikTok, Google, LinkedIn and others) and the brand's category rules: the copy, on-image or on-screen text, pictures and people. Rewrites what can be fixed honestly, adds the disclosures that are needed, and flags anything that needs a human or legal review, with one pass, fixed or flag line per ad and platform. Use alone when you already have the ad text or images and know where they will run; otherwise run the playbook for the job (e.g. make-static-ads, make-content, email-lifecycle).

skills.name: ads-north-star-strategy
skills.description: Turn a brand's facts, a campaign brief and the product into a one-minute Meta ad strategy with its reasoning — goal, audience, objective and placements, budget split, how many ads and how different they must be (generate 3x so the user can choose), the test frame, the success metric, and safety rules for the user to accept. Decides what launch-meta-ad-campaign then executes, and re-reads the strategy after a deep check to show which assumption changed. Use it after intake and before any creative is generated or any campaign is built.

features: a one-minute strategy with the reason behind every choice
objective chosen from the business outcome, with an honest bridge when the host cannot launch it
one ad set on small budgets; 2-3 ads that differ in argument, generated at 3x so the user can choose
test frame and success metric with a threshold from the unit economics
safety rules proposed, saved only once accepted
re-read after a deep check names the assumption that changed
metadata.example_prompt: We have $1,500 for three weeks to get demo requests. What should the Meta ads strategy be?

skills.name: analyze-performance
skills.description: Weekly performance read across every channel we run: what worked, why, and what to make next, judged on the business's real number (store revenue, qualified pipeline, retained users), not platform claims. Use when: write my Monday report; how are my ads doing — which ad won?; are my ads actually making money (Meta says 4x ROAS but revenue is flat); why did sales drop this week; did the test win; is my tracking working; monthly numbers for the replan; anything on fire today. Not for acting on the recommendations (pausing, scaling, launching) — use run-paid-campaigns; not for replanning the budget — use plan-campaign.

skills.name: review-ugc-render
skills.description: Mandatory pre-publish review gate for a UGC video render. Transcribes the finished render's AUDIO with Whisper and word-diffs it against the approved spoken script, then gates keeping the render as the final version (video_review) — blocking a render whose generated audio mis-voices a word (e.g. the approved "human-vetted" spoken as "human witted"), says a different number or brand name, flips a negation, drops an approved phrase, or comes back silent. Full pages go to make-content; paid search goes to run-paid-campaigns.

skills.name: make-content
skills.description: Writes marketing content: articles, single posts, newsletters, scripts and repurposed cuts, each with an edit note and a claims check. Words only; nothing is invented or published. Not for a dated posting calendar — use run-organic-social; not ad copy (make-static-ads) or promo emails (email-lifecycle). Press releases, landing and product pages, and sales decks are not covered.

skills.name: plan-campaign
skills.description: Campaign planner: turns a product, offer, goal, budget and date into a plan the marketer can approve and a designer can start from today, with every channel kept or dropped for a reason. Zero paid is a valid answer; it never spends. Use when the ask names a campaign, a launch, drop or season push, a budget or a date: I have this budget and a launch date — what do I run, where?; plan my launch, drop or Black Friday push; plan a campaign; how should I split $5k; plan next month's campaign; our CAC blew up — replan. Not for a broad "grow my brand", "get more customers" or "where do I start" with no campaign, budget or date — use where-to-start; not for pausing ads on a sold-out product — use run-paid-campaigns; not for an email-only send plan — use email-lifecycle; not for reading this week's numbers — use analyze-performance.

skills.description: Audience research: who the buyers are, in their own words, where they gather and how to reach them — plus named prospect lists when asked. Use when the marketer says "research our audience", "who should we target", "mine our reviews", "why do people buy us or leave", "where does our audience hang out"; or for lists: "find 50 right-fit leads with emails", "find retailers or accounts to pitch", "score these leads / who do we call first", "who's looking for an alternative to X", "tell me when a past champion changes jobs". Not for market size or trends — use research-market; not for writing the messages — use write-outreach.

skills.name: research-competitors

Delivers a readable report saved to the brand, so the next run reports what changed. Never copies their words or disparages them. Not for what people say about you or your market — use research-market; not for who your buyers are — use research-audience.

skills.name: research-market
